## Solution

**Claim:** The minimum value is $1$.

**Upper bound.** Take $p(z) = z^n \in P$. Then for $|z| = 1$, $|p(z)| = |z|^n = 1$, so $\max_{|z|=1}|p(z)| = 1$. Hence
$$\min_{p \in P}\max_{|z|=1}|p(z)| \le 1.$$

**Lower bound.** Let $p(z) = z^n + a_{n-1}z^{n-1} + \cdots + a_0$ be any monic polynomial of degree $n$, so the leading coefficient is $a_n = 1$. For $z = e^{i\theta}$ on the unit circle, by Parseval's identity (or the mean-value property of the $L^2$ norm on the circle),
$$\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi} |p(e^{i\theta})|^2\,d\theta = \sum_{k=0}^{n} |a_k|^2.$$
Since $p$ is monic, $|a_n|^2 = 1$, and all terms are non-negative, so
$$\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi} |p(e^{i\theta})|^2\,d\theta = \sum_{k=0}^{n}|a_k|^2 \ge |a_n|^2 = 1.$$

The maximum of a continuous function is at least its average (in fact $\max |p|^2 \ge \text{average of }|p|^2$), so
$$\max_{|z|=1}|p(z)|^2 \ge \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}|p(e^{i\theta})|^2\,d\theta \ge 1,$$
which gives $\max_{|z|=1}|p(z)| \ge 1$.

Since this holds for every $p \in P$,
$$\min_{p \in P}\max_{|z|=1}|p(z)| \ge 1.$$

**Conclusion.** Combining both bounds,
$$\min_{p \in P}\max_{|z|=1}|p(z)| = 1,$$
with equality attained uniquely (up to the lower coefficients being zero) by $p(z) = z^n$.

### PROOF COMPLETE
